title: Unregistered sale agreements - the enforceability questions
p1: Many people believe that a sale agreement is useless if it is not registered. But the reality is more nuanced. An unregistered agreement may still create important legal consequences in certain situations.
p2: The common misconception is that registration decides everything. In many cases, a written sale agreement can show the understanding between parties, even if it does not by itself transfer ownership of the property. The surprising part? A document that cannot prove ownership transfer may still be relevant evidence in a legal dispute.
p3: Registration and enforceability are two different questions. Registration mainly relates to giving legal recognition and public notice to certain transactions, while enforceability depends on factors like the terms of the agreement, applicable law, and the facts of the case. The practical lesson: never assume an unregistered agreement has no value, but also do not treat it as a complete substitute for a registered sale deed.
